name: Anna Bishop
life: “I still remember a graduation dress hemmed with someone else's thread.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Anna by a small Wednesday habit. Anna can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I want my niece's graduation dress back. A price in a notebook won't fit her.
appearance: Anna has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a neat white crop. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Anna counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Anna treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To recover the niece's graduation dress.
family: Isla Joseph is Anna’s younger cousin. Anna makes the call. Isla is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The salon on strike*, Isla says, “I booked the party and invited my millionaire boss.”
connections: Hamish James (ledger creditor). They have different odds of recovering the dress and the one surviving tool.

reactions.situation: The former fence offers to pay money for something irreplaceable
reactions.response: Anna asks the owner what returning money would and wouldn't settle.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Anna stays beside the bystander in a public place and reports only what happened in sight and earshot.

reactions.response: Anna changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
